An executed test-vector suite (Document ID TV-RREQ-FDE-2026-V1) evaluating whether a standard 4-valued FDE/Belnap-Dunn kernel satisfies the R_req Tier-P1 distinctions: PARTIAL FAIL on Knowledge Status (collapses Underdetermined into Unknown), FAIL on Justification Mode (no lineage without annotation), FAIL on Currency (no native temporal tracking), PASS on Absence-of-Evidence-vs-Evidence-of-Absence (native N vs F distinction). Overall verdict: FDE is necessary but insufficient as a standalone KnowledgeOS kernel; requires wrapping in an Annotated/Graded Labeled Frame Space.

An extended, 'ratification-ready' edition of R_req adding a Structural Completeness Theorem and proof sketch (sufficiency/minimality/closure argument for the distinction set), three new distinctions (Explicit-vs-Implicit D-1.3, Analytic-vs-Synthetic D-5.1, Necessary-vs-Contingent-Modality D-5.2), a per-distinction tractability/complexity matrix, deep integration specifications with Contr/Zero/Evaluation, a four-phase governance workflow, and a closing 'RATIFY R_req v1.0' recommendation, under Document ID SPEC-RREQ-2026-V1-RATIFIED.

A concrete kernel architecture proposal (SPEC-ABK-2026-V1) extending standard 4-valued FDE by pairing each proposition's FDE valuation (nu) with a justification DAG (J), a temporal validity window (tau: start/end/dependency-version-vector/TTL), and modal/scope metadata (mu: Analytic-vs-Synthetic, Necessary-vs-Contingent, scope bitmask), forming a 4-tuple State(phi)=<nu,J,tau,mu>; defines Knowledge Order (<=_k) and Truth Order (<=_t) plus lattice conjunction/disjunction operators combining valuation, justification-DAG union, temporal intersection and metadata AND; includes a full TypeScript reference implementation (ABKState, ABKAlgebra) and reports 100% pass on the SPEC-RREQ-TEST-2026-V1 suite (resolving the four failures found for bare FDE: Underdetermined-vs-Unknown, Inferred-vs-Assumed, Stale-vs-Expired).

A corrective reformulation of R_req making it context/question-relative rather than a fixed universal set: R_req(Q,Gamma) subseteq D (the distinctions required to answer question Q under context Gamma), Adequacy(R,Q,Gamma) iff R_req(Q,Gamma) subseteq Preserved(R,Gamma), and Loss_req(pi,Q,Gamma) = R_req(Q,Gamma) intersect Collapsed(pi) as a required-information-loss metric (Loss_req=empty as the strong adequacy condition). Distilled into eight core propositions RREQ-1..RREQ-8 (Requiredness, Preservation, Collapse, Adequacy, Projection, Required Information Loss, Transformation Change, Reasoning-System Properties) proposed as the artifact KR-RREQ-2026-09, superseding a prior document's universal/literature-grounded R_req and its direct R_req->KernelSelection governance chain.

A self-contained ratification declaration (Document 5 of the KnowledgeOS Ratification Package) issuing five commitments -- Tier P1 immutability, an Extension Protocol requiring test vectors/tractability proof/2-3 HPA approval, a Loss_{R_req}(pi)=0 compliance requirement for P1 distinctions, a redefinition of Zero as formal compliance with R_req, and a redefinition of Contr as detected via D-1.1 and managed via the ABK-Contr Bridge -- and a fully-checked ratification-status block recommending RATIFY for R_req v1.0, ABK-1 v1.0, and ABK-Contr v1.0, signed '[HPA Supervisory]', dated 2026-09-02.

A self-declared [RATIFIED] R_req specification using a six-invariant taxonomy distinct in notation and count from this batch's earlier D-1.x/Tier-P1/P2/P3 R_req inventory: R-INV-01 Standing (S+ != S-), R-INV-02 Boundary (Explicit != Derived), R-INV-03 State (Contr != Underdetermined), R-INV-04 Provenance (P_i != P_j), R-INV-05 Temporal/Context, R-INV-06 Reasoning Parameter (S(depth) != S(default)); defines Collapse(rho,s_i,s_j) as an Epistemic Fault when (s_i,s_j) in R_req, and three compliance verification tests (Identity Preservation, Provenance Traceability, Boundary Differentiation).

A self-declared [RATIFIED] Contradiction Isolation & Resolution Semantics spec: Contr(p) iff S+(p)>0 and S-(p)>0 within a context, distinguished by threshold tau from Underdetermined (S+=S-=0) and Uncertain (small positive S+, S-=0); a five-type contradiction typology (Direct, Source, Rule, Observation, Interpretation) each with a formal triggering condition; a non-explosion postulate defining an isolation-scope closure Contr_scope(p) = {p} union Dependents(p) union ConflictingSources(p); a four-state lifecycle (DETECTED->ISOLATED->TRIAGED->RESOLVED); and four named resolution operators (Supersede, Contextualize, Retract, Discount) each with a formal signature and effect, plus a Python ContradictionEngine reference implementation.

A self-declared [RATIFIED] Evaluation Semantics spec defining EVal as a 5-tuple <Standing,Boundary,Reason,Context,Provenance>: Standing=(S+,S-) in R+xR+ with S+ != 1-S- (no scalar collapse); Boundary in {EXPLICIT,DERIVED,HYPOTHETICAL}; Reason as a justification DAG/proof; Context=<t,d,theta>; Provenance a DAG of source attributions. Derives a four-way EpistemicState (ACCEPTED/REFUTED/CONTRADICTION/UNDERDETERMINED) via threshold comparison of S+ and S- against context-defined tau+/tau-, and states three operational-law properties: Non-Destructive Composition (standings add rather than cancel across unioned state graphs), Non-Monotonicity of Standing (new evidence need not preserve prior evaluation), and Scope Isolation (contradiction in one context does not force contradiction in an orthogonal context); includes a full Python reference implementation (Standing, EvaluationResult, EvaluationEngine).

A self-declared [RATIFIED] Determination Semantics spec: Det maps an EVal tuple E and a policy threshold vector tau=<tau_accept+,tau_refute-,tau_margin,omega_prov> to a 4-field DeterminationValue <d_state,d_action,d_confidence,d_prov_ref>; d_state is one of DETERMINED_TRUE/DETERMINED_FALSE/DETERMINED_CONTRADICTION/UNDERDETERMINED/AMBIGUOUS via a piecewise threshold comparison of S+/S-/margin; each state maps to an operational action (EXECUTE/HALT-REJECT/ESCALATE/DEFER/DEFER respectively); enforces the explicit non-conflation Det(E) != Truth != Knowledge != Belief; supports partial determination via an explicit UnmetThresholds vector when provenance weight is insufficient; includes a Python DeterminationEngine reference implementation.

notations: delta: S_rep x O_core x CTX -> S_rep x M_trace
note: A self-declared [RATIFIED] Transition Semantics spec: delta(R,op,C) -> <R',mu> where mu is a metadata trace (TxID, Timestamp, ActorID, pre/post state hashes, provenance delta); requires three formal properties for every transition -- Non-Destructiveness (Nodes(R) subseteq Nodes(R'), no historical assertion or provenance edge may be destroyed without an explicit tombstone/supersedes relation), Invariant Closure (R satisfying the core invariant set implies R' does too), and Determinism (identical inputs produce identical output states); classifies transitions into three operational classes (Additive delta_+ for ASSERT/LINK, Revision delta_rev for REVISE/REFACTOR adding a SUPERSEDES edge while retaining the old claim, Retraction delta_- for RETRACT which updates standing rather than deleting nodes); asserts a reversibility postulate (an inverse delta^-1 exists that appends a counter-record rather than erasing history); includes a Python StateTransitionEngine copy-on-write reference implementation.

A proposed missing bridge concept between representation-adequacy theory and kernel theory: EA(K,O,Q,Gamma) holds when the representation K and operations O together can answer the required questions Q while preserving every required distinction and producing an auditable transition. Explicitly motivated by the observation that a representation (e.g. ABK-1) can be perfectly Adequate(R,Q,Gamma) while still being insufficient as a kernel, because Adequacy says nothing about whether the required operations, transitions, and auditability actually exist over that representation.

note: Closes CLOSURE-1 (EVal) and CLOSURE-2 (Det) together. EVal is redefined as an explicitly PARTIAL function K x P x Gamma -rightharpoonup <Standing,Boundary,Reason,Context,Provenance,EvalStatus>, with Standing generalized to a triple <S+,S-,ambiguity mu> whose aggregation is delegated to a parameterizable operator (not fixed addition), and three named non-total failure modes (undefined proposition, epistemic-firewall-trapped, incomplete-context/non-decidable). Det:EVal x Q x Gamma -> Determination (a 4-tuple Status/ConfidenceInterval/RiskProfile/Actionability) is specified with three separation axioms: Non-Collapsing (identical EVal may yield different Determinations under different queries Q), Firewall Isolation Invariant (a ContradictionTrapped EVal must yield UndeterminedConflict with Actionability in {RequiresHumanReview,Blocked}), and Task-Bounded Sufficiency (positive determination iff available evidence satisfies R_req(Q,Gamma)). Includes a Python EpistemicEngine reference implementation and a passing three-part test (partiality, non-collapsing, firewall-blocks-actionability).

Closes CLOSURE-3 (each of the 5 O_core primitives given a formal <Pre,Post,Persist,Prov> tuple contract, plus the monotonicity axiom Nodes(K_t) subseteq Nodes(delta(K_t,o,Gamma))) and CLOSURE-4 together: parameterized semantic equivalence K1 equiv_sem^{Q,Gamma,O} K2 iff Det(EVal(K1,q,Gamma),q,Gamma)=Det(EVal(K2,q,Gamma),q,Gamma) for every query q and operation o, plus a composition algebra for o2-after-o1 with three named properties -- Non-Commutativity in general (RETRACT-after-ASSERT != ASSERT-after-RETRACT), Orthogonal Commutativity (operations with disjoint targets commute up to semantic equivalence), and Idempotency of Isolation (ISOLATE(p) composed with itself is semantically equivalent to a single ISOLATE(p)).

The first actual comparative kernel-selection act in this batch's closure cascade: four named candidate architectures are evaluated against the four-dimension Executable Adequacy matrix (Psi_Soundness/Isolation/Termination/Determinism) -- K-FLAT (flat RDF triples) REJECTED for collapsing provenance and permitting global explosion; K-FDE (pure FDE bilattice) REJECTED for scalar collapse despite preserving truth values; K-REL (relational projections) REJECTED for join explosion despite preserving schema and scoped constraints; ABK-1 (Attributed Bipartite Graph) passes all four dimensions and is declared 'the unique minimal Kernel Architecture satisfying EA', with a Python ExecutableAdequacyEvaluator harness and a passing test.

notations: A Theory-critical, B Theory-parameterized, C Implementation obligation, D Empirical obligation, E Governance obligation
Theory Closed iff no unresolved A-items remain
note: A proposed five-way classification for every remaining open item in a theory-closure effort: A Theory-critical (if unresolved, the meaning of the theory is undefined), B Theory-parameterized (the theory deliberately allows multiple valid implementations/semantics), C Implementation obligation (the theory is defined but implementation must demonstrate it), D Empirical obligation (theory defined, real-world evidence still required), E Governance obligation (theory cannot decide it; governance must). Closure criterion: Theory Closed iff no unresolved A-items remain. Proposed to replace repeated ad hoc C1-C4-style closure attempts with a single classificatory gate artifact THEORY-CLOSURE-GATE-2026-v1.0.

note: The document that applies the A-E theory-criticality classification definitively to every KnowledgeOS kernel component, declares KnowledgeOS Kernel Theory v1.3 THEORETICALLY CLOSED because zero unresolved Category-A items remain, and freezes six constitutional axioms: (1) Pipeline Separation Truth!=EVal!=Det!=GovernanceAction; (2) Non-Explosion under Contradiction (a local Contr(p) does not entail deriving every q); (3) Representation Adequacy (Adequate(K,Q,Gamma) iff R_req(Q,Gamma) subseteq Distinctions(K)); (4) History-Preserving State Evolution (V(K_t) subseteq V(K_{t+1}) and H(K_t) subseteq H(K_{t+1}) for every O_core operation); (5) Existential Query Sensitivity (for every valid K there exist at least two queries whose determinations differ); (6) Governance Boundary Decoupling (Determination=<Status,DeterminationBound,RiskProfile> contains zero governance/Actionability fields). An executed experiment (research/knowledgeos-sim/kos12/fde/, verdict at results/fde/verdict.md) testing four candidate contradiction/missingness representations (Classical {P,not-P}, K3 {T,F,U}, FDE (S+,S-), and Standing x Boundary x Context x Provenance) against 13 required distinctions: Classical preserves 1/collapses 1/cannot-represent 11 (not adequate); K3 preserves 3/collapses 10 (not adequate); FDE (S+,S-) preserves 11/collapses 2 (not adequate -- NoEvidence=Absent and InsufficientEvidence=Underdetermined both collapse); only the four-component Standing x Boundary x Context x Provenance preserves all 13 (adequate). Also finds a positive Standing (1,0) covers five distinct scenarios (PositiveEvidence, NotAssessed, Underdetermined, InsufficientEvidence, TheoryIncomplete) equally boundary-ambiguous as an empty (0,0) Standing, and concludes the missing channel across every Standing class is 'reason', not only at (0,0).

An exhaustive search over all 16384 subsets of a 14-operator set under a declared 25-capability model: the 13-operator baseline C0 fails its own baseline (21/25 capabilities, 9/16 scenarios); the missing power is Qualify:Observation x Policy -rightharpoonup Evidence (already carried by the corpus as gap G1); exactly two minimal kernels exist, both cardinality 13, differing only in packaging; 14 powers are irreducible but only 12 of 14 operators are; DetectGap is derivable in 12/12 admissible representations with no smuggling detected; under every audit reduction granted, |K_min| falls from 13 to 8 across four minimal kernels forming a six-operator core; 7/7 semantic-smuggling absorption probes were REJECTED. The experiment's own follow-up self-supersedes its headline via a Reachability != Epistemic-adequacy finding, reordering the research programme to Representation -> Capability -> Reachability -> Minimality and moving the kernel-minimality question from first to seventh in a seven-level hierarchy.

The cross-theory synthesis verdict consolidating a five-external-theory (DEL, Belief Revision, Probability, Information Theory, Statistical Decision Theory) vs ten-KnowledgeOS-concept compatibility investigation: none of the five theories is individually compatible, they partition the ten concepts almost disjointly (none covers more than three), four theory-adoptions would each delete a specific existing boxed corpus result by assuming a consistency/veridicality condition KnowledgeOS deliberately refuses, and the strongest corroboration found (Q_t~=A_i, awareness structures) was a self-corroboration the corpus already owned five days before connecting it. Produces a comparison matrix, 11 exact correspondences, and 25 falsifiable hypotheses across the five theory-comparison documents.

A twelve-class taxonomy used to classify every construct's remaining readiness gap: D derivation, DEF definition, A architecture, S semantic, O operation, T transformation, E evidence, I implementation, TEST testability, EC empirical, G governance, B book -- applied across the 25-construct master matrix, showing Architecture affects 16 of 25 constructs, Governance affects 24 of 25 (all but Policy), and Operation propagates from a single construct (O_core) to every operation cell in the matrix.

A formal intake framework (GN-95) classifying any artifact claiming governance status as A (Authoritative Act, requiring all nine of act id/date/authority/exact decision/affected canonical artifact/before state/after state/proving governance record/source location), or otherwise as B/C (advisory)/F (internally contradictory, forcing rejection regardless of recording status). Applied to all September 2026 KnowledgeOS material: zero artifacts qualify as A; four claimed acts (DECISION-01, factivity R1, a Z-deferral, and an FR-001 freeze, all in theory-v1.2-simulation/) would qualify as A if a governance record existed but are unrecorded AND independently self-contradictory (forcing Classification F); a separate 'Hilbert ruling' is classified C (Advisory).
